statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is in the low band because the market is closed for the weekend and Friday's final session retraced rather than extending one-way; Stress stays high on unresolved rates, energy and geopolitical tension.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. No evidence-based danger window applies inside this window because every hour falls within the CME weekend halt. The first live structural test arrives with the 22:00Z Sunday reopen and Monday's ISM Services PMI, both outside this horizon.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a record close through the weekend halt, with Friday's completed retracement keeping Tail low and Stress high
body: Assessment made during the CME equity index futures weekend halt. Futures settled at 21:00Z on 2 October and do not reopen until 22:00Z on 4 October, which is roughly 22 hours after this forecast window closes, so no live NQ price path exists in any of the 24 hours assessed. Friday's final session is therefore the governing evidence. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, after printing an intraday all-time high of 31,017.53 and then giving back about 0.68% into the close on a day range of 30,737.07 to 31,017.53. That give-back is the decisive observation under this contract: September payrolls missed badly at +29,000 against roughly 90,000 expected, with August revised down to +133,000, average hourly earnings up only 0.1% on the month and the unemployment rate ticking up to 4.2%, yet the tape produced an orderly advance that retraced rather than a no-retracement extension. Implied volatility confirmed the decay, with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31 and settling at its session low. Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than aligns: the 10-year yield collapsed to roughly 5.17% immediately after the labour data and then reversed to close at 5.2939%, while the 30-year finished at 5.6448% near cycle highs, even as traders cut October rate-hike odds to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier. Energy eased but stayed expensive, with WTI printing a one-month low near 88.06 on the G7 announcement of a release of up to 100 million barrels through the IEA before recovering to settle about 91.41, and Brent near 102. The Iran conflict remains a persistent stalemate rather than a fresh discontinuity, with roughly 30 drone and 10 anti-ship missile attacks per week on Hormuz shipping and at least 13 vessels struck since mid-September, while flows recover partly through routes that bypass the strait. A record equity level alongside a long end at cycle highs is a genuine tension, and conflicting cross-asset evidence raises Stress and tempers Confidence under this contract; it does not establish the persistent one-way structure, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements that Tail measures. With the market shut there is no mechanism for mean-reversion failure inside the window, so Tail stays in the low band throughout, easing to 8 across the Saturday dead zone before a token rise to 10 in the closing hours as a full day of weekend information accumulates unpriced.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span 2 October from 01:00Z plus the first hour of 3 October. Published Claude assessments held Tail at 20 through the Asian and European hours, lifted it to 23-24 as the pre-payrolls advance built, and peaked at 25 and 27 in the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots immediately after the +29,000 payrolls print, the only orange hours of the day. Tail then fell back to 22-23 across the U.S. afternoon as the move retraced, and dropped to 14, 12, 11 and 9 in the final four hours once the record close was in and futures entered the weekend halt. Stress stayed high all day in a 68-79 band and Confidence held between 84 and 89.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this window falls inside the CME weekend halt, and the 22:00Z Sunday reopen sits roughly 22 hours beyond its close, so no price path can form and Tail stays in the low band throughout. Tail eases to 8 across the Saturday dead zone and rises only to 10 in the closing hours as a full day of unpriced weekend information accumulates. Stress eases from 66 to about 62 by mid-Saturday as the payrolls catalyst resolves and oil comes off its highs, then firms back to 67 on the unreconciled pairing of a record equity level with a 30-year yield near cycle highs. Confidence declines from 83 to 78 purely because the live price-path component ages with no weekend session to replace it. The characterisation is normal while the tape is shut and turns mixed in the final hours, where the operative feature is the conflict between a soft labour print with sharply lower hike odds and a long end holding near cycle highs. The first genuine tests are the Sunday reopen and Monday's ISM Services PMI, followed by the September FOMC minutes on Wednesday and a 30-year auction on Thursday.
